newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican superhero "certifies" U.S. as drug-crazed.
newsitem.headline: Mexican superhero "certifies" U.S. as drug-crazed.

text.p: One of Mexico's most popular social activists on Friday "certified" the United States as the world's top drug consumer, posting a diploma on iron bars outside the U.S. embassy in Mexico City.
SuperBarrio, a masked and costumed wrestler and advocate for the poor in Mexico, made his protest as controversy over the U.S. "certification" of Mexico as an ally in its war on drugs simmered.

Wearing his trademark costume -- part comic hero Spiderman, part wrestling star Hulk Hogan -- SuperBarrio noted the "invaluable participation in supervising drug quality" on the part of the United States.

Meanwhile, a small group of protesters shouted, "The druggies are the gringos" as a couple, wearing masks depicting U.S. President Bill Clinton and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, looked on.
Superbarrio's action was an ironic response to controversy in Mexico City and Washington over the certification process.
Clinton certified last week that Mexico is a cooperative ally in the war on drugs, despite opposition from critics of Mexican drug corruption especially in the U.S. Congress.
SuperBarrio has spawned a cottage indusry of costumed social advocates. Others such as SuperEcology and SuperGay have followed in his path.
There was no immediate complaint from the White House about Mexican meddling in U.S. affairs.
